item.title: Hear why a bus shelter pilot was paused
item.summary: A planning interview separates a design decision from an incomplete evaluation.
item.transcript_text:
Host: The shelter pilot seems to have failed. Two stops have already gone back to their old layouts.
Planner: Those stops were chosen because they flood. Then a nearby road closure doubled the number of buses turning past them. Drivers had trouble seeing through the new side panel after dark.
Host: Would a clear panel solve that?
Planner: It might. A clear panel produces glare under some streetlights. We have built a full-sized model so drivers and wheelchair users can try alternatives under controlled lighting. After that, we'll take the most promising version back to a stop. I also want to test it on a road that hasn't been affected by the closure.
Host: So taking out the panels was one decision. The final design is still open.

questions.prompt: What distinction does the planner make?
options: An immediate removal differs from a final design decision
Only flooded sites should ever be tested
A mock-up can replace every field test
An interim solution always becomes permanent
questions.explanation: The panels came out, but the planner is still investigating designs.

questions.prompt: How did the road closure complicate interpretation?
options: It disconnected the shelter lights
It made the drivers avoid both routes
It flooded the trial sites directly
It changed the traffic going past the shelters

questions.prompt: What risk comes with a transparent panel?
options: Reduced visibility in all conditions
No driver can see through it at all
Light reflections in some conditions
It floods before the opaque version
questions.explanation: The planner identifies glare as a conditional issue.

options: It makes field sites unnecessary
Users can compare options under controlled lighting
It removes the need to ask drivers
It guarantees flood resistance
questions.explanation: The model lets users test alternatives under deliberately set conditions.

questions.prompt: Why test beyond the affected road?
options: To separate some traffic effects from layout effects
To avoid evaluating turning buses
To make the different panels impossible to compare
To prove changes always improve safety
questions.explanation: A second site reduces the influence of the unusual diversion.
